# Resume thesis implementation

The working session for `research/regression-testing/`. Run on the Fable tier:
this session makes design decisions, fuses components, and reviews what cheaper
sessions produced.

## Read

`research/regression-testing/CLAUDE.md` (and the root `CLAUDE.md` it inherits),
`docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`.

Read `docs/event-model.md` if the next task touches logging. Read the manuscript
only where a task's spec names a section, via
`python tools/manuscript.py --section <n>` — it is a `.docx` and cannot be
opened with Read.

## Report first

Before doing any work, state in a few lines:

- what is done, in progress and blocked, per phase
- **what is waiting on the author** — open questions blocking tasks, shortest
  first. This is the only thing the user can act on while you work, so it goes
  near the top
- what you are about to do

## Then work

Take the next `[FABLE]` task whose dependencies are met.

Where the next ready tasks are `[STANDARD]`, dispatch them to the
`thesis-standard` subagent (pinned to Opus 5) rather than writing them yourself,
then review what comes back against the spec before marking anything done.

Three things about dispatching:

- **Dispatch in batches, not one at a time.** This session is Fable-priced;
  orchestration with narration between each dispatch is the expensive way to do
  cheap work.
- **A subagent starts cold.** If a `[STANDARD]` spec is not self-contained, do
  not paste context around it to make the dispatch work — the task was
  mis-tiered. Either tighten the spec in the plan, or retag it `[FABLE]`.
- **Do not delegate trivial work.** A subagent spinning up to write ten lines
  costs more than writing them inline. Delegation pays on substantial units.

Reviewing dispatched work is not optional and is not a glance. It is the
`[FABLE]` half of the tiering argument the thesis makes, and it leaves a record
— see `/thesis-review` for the dedicated pass and `REVIEW_LOG.md` for the
format. A batch reviewed inside this session gets an entry there too.

## Record as you go

- **Task status** in `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, as it changes, not at the end.
- **Decisions** in `DECISIONS.md`: what, when, why, and by whom. `Decided by:
  agent` is only for choices `CLAUDE.md` lists under "do not ask about".
  Anything on the stop-and-ask list is the author's.
- **New questions** in `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`, with options, trade-off and a
  recommendation. Never remove an entry; move it to Resolved when it is ruled on.
- **Implementation log entries** where a task proved substantially harder than
  estimated, forced a design change, or bears on a claim in Chapter 2. Apply the
  filter in the file: would it change how someone else built this? A debugging
  session does not qualify. **Omit rather than pad** — a thin log is an honest
  finding, and §3.7 can say so.

## Stop and ask

Everything on the stop-and-ask list in `CLAUDE.md`: what is logged, what counts
as a pass, any threshold, model selection, anything needing a simulation re-run
to undo, anything the manuscript leaves unspecified, and anything that would
change how the application handles a request. Present the options, state the
trade-off, recommend one, and wait.

## Finish by reporting

What changed, what needs a decision, and what the next session picks up.
